clue.text: Transcribe date inaccurately, being poorly focused on the task?

indicators.note: copying something inaccurately jumbles it, so these two words have their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless clerk copies a date wrongly because their mind has wandered from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurately' rearranges the fourteen letters of TRANSCRIBE and DATE; 'being' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disorganised and forgetful, whose attention drifts from the work in hand, is described as scatty or harebrained.

clue.text: Scot getting round gentleman always on the up — creeping for promotion?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
the Scottish name surrounds the other two pieces, so it is a container signal

parts.note: Mac is a stock crossword name for a Scotsman
Sir is the title of a knighted gentleman
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A Scotsman who keeps sucking up to the boss is always angling to climb the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting round' builds MSIREERAC, and 'on the up' reads that whole run upwards, as a down entry allows; 'creeping' is sucking up, not moving slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition pursued for personal advancement at work, often by currying favour, is the sense; the question mark marks the playful paraphrase.

clue.text: Any number wearing classical garb in Pacific kingdom

parts.note: the toga was the robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome

clue.text: Acquit former partner, individual to think highly of

clue.text: Victims in casks such as the one that did for Clarence?

definitions.meaning: the targets of jokes or ridicule are the ... of them

definitions.text: casks such as the one that did for Clarence?
definitions.meaning: large barrels for wine or beer; the Duke of Clarence was said to have been drowned in a butt of malmsey wine

explanation.surface: Victims are found inside barrels, like the one that famously finished off a royal duke.
explanation.walkthrough: George, Duke of Clarence, brother of Edward IV, was reputedly drowned in a barrel of malmsey in 1478, as Shakespeare shows in Richard III.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: people who are made fun of, and big wooden barrels for liquor.

clue.text: Spartan is in struggle with the hopefuls

clue.text: Born dreadfully devoid of things possessed, wanting much

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Poor people lacking the necessities of life, in great want, are described as impoverished or deprived.

clue.text: Philosopher making point about notion not quite right

parts.note: a dot is a small point

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the notion; 'about' wraps the point around the trimmed notion plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was the French Enlightenment thinker who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Impression made by Oxford?

clue.text: A non-drinking worker must go round boundary as a guard

the worker ant is a crossword stalwart

clue.text: Supply me a stand, for ultimately I must sell stuff

explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper or merchant would say this of himself, because a trader's job is to sell goods.
